liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): Scarlet into Fire runs about half an hour in the second set; Scarlet>Fire is very good, with heavy psychedelic feel [9][14]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): Opening song cited as showcase of the audience tape's quality [17]
- **Cumberland Blues** (1 review): First set rocks, with Cumberland Blues singled out [13]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (1 review): Reviewer felt disconnected from the first set until Fire On The Mountain arrived [11]
- **Playin' In The Band** (1 review): Scarlet>Fire is long and psychedelic, with an exceptional Playin' following [13]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): A strong jam follows Terrapin [9]
- **Drums** (1 review): The drums segment sounds especially powerful [9]

## The recordings

- **gd81-10-08.sbd.macdonald.7918.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 176 min; rated 3.73/5 by 11 [1]. Said about its sound: Soundboard mix is uneven: Jerry's vocals often inaudible, Phil's bass and Bob's guitar missing, levels fluctuating constantly; Soundboard quality is typical for the era and sounds fine to this reviewer; Sound is not great, but works as background listening; a better copy would help [10][12][13][14][18]
- **gd1981-10-08.sbd.128681.MrBill.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 173 min; rated 2.2/5 by 5 [3]. Said about its sound: Soundboard is an upgrade, but the playback deck limits upper-frequency response; a Nak deck would help [16]
- **gd1981-10-08.151700.sbd.hance.sirmick.flac24**: soundboard; 21 songs; 174 min [4]. Said about its sound: Pitch adjusted, gain surges in CC Rider and Cumberland smoothed, and Jerry's guitar rebalanced because it was low [4]
- **gd1981-10-08.170655.aud.lamarre.vernon.andrewF.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 174 min [6]
- **gd1981-10-08.aud.partial.stankiewicz.126105.flac1644**: audience recording; 12 songs; 94 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [8]. Said about its sound: Stankiewicz audience tape beats the soundboard for fidelity, capturing a hollow, empty-sounding theater; tape 2 is missing [17]

## Around the show

- Breaks the pattern of the previous year and a half of shows, with exploratory, jammy playing [15]
- The following night's recording has better sound quality than this one [15]
- Playing is slow and uninspired, unlike tight slower-tempo shows the reviewer enjoys [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd81-10-08.sbd.macdonald.7918.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard chain: CM to cassette to DAT to CDR, via Neil Sturvetant, John Martin, Alasdair Macdonald; seeded by Matt Vernon [1]
- **gd1981-10-08.sbd.128681.MrBill.flac16**: transferred by Bill Guarneri; source: Recording and transfer info SBD > CM > C; C > Pioneer deck > wav > Sound Forge 10 > TLH > flac [3]
- **gd1981-10-08.151700.sbd.hance.sirmick.flac24**: transferred by John Hance & SIRMick; source: Soundboard Cassette (1st gen) [4]. Also: Source from John Hance; tape flips patched using the Stankiewicz audience source, shnid 126105 [4]
- **gd1981-10-08.170655.aud.lamarre.vernon.andrewF.flac2496**: taped by Unknown from the collection of Doug Lamarre; transferred by Matt Vernon, Andrew F; source: Analog Audience Source: Unknown mic/deck/generation [6]. Also: This audience source differs from 126105 and 152229, and is patched with pieces from both [6]
- **gd1981-10-08.aud.partial.stankiewicz.126105.flac1644**: taped by Richie Stankiewicz; transferred by Richie Stankiewicz and Andrew F.; source: Partial, AUD: 2x Beyer M-88 > Sony TC-D5, center floor area, MAC. [8]
